newsitem.title: USA: Ohio egg supplier denies it sold old eggs.
newsitem.headline: Ohio egg supplier denies it sold old eggs.

text.p: A large egg supplier that distributes to stores in 18 U.S. states and overseas has denied allegations, made in a lawsuit filed this week, that the company sold eggs with deceptive freshness dates.

In the suit filed Tuesday in federal court in Toledo, Ohio, privately-held AgriGeneral Co. L.P. was accused of routinely storing unsold eggs, then repackaging them with fresh ones labeled with new sell-by dates.

The suit, which also charged AgriGeneral with failing to pay overtime wages, was brought by the Ohio Public Interest Research Group, a consumer watchdog organization, and 25 current and former employees of the company.

AgriGeneral, which said its annual sales were $88 million, sells eggs under various labels in the United States, Canada, Mexico, Europe, the Far East and Middle East. It has about 430 workers at two plants in small towns near Columbus in central Ohio.
The Croton, Ohio-based company disputed the suit's claims.

"The allegations made regarding the quality of eggs processed and shipped by AgriGeneral are unsubstantiated and ludicrous," the company said in a statement. A spokeswoman said company officials declined an interview with Reuters.

In a letter to companies that buy its eggs, AgriGeneral said, "It is an absolute misstatement of fact to assert that we pack old eggs." It also said the suit "amounts to false accounts made by disgruntled former and current employees and, we believe, is motivated by outside efforts to organize our employees" into labor unions.
Mark Finnegan, a lawyer for the plaintiffs, said he was unaware of any union organizing efforts.
The suit seeks back pay for workers and $200 each or other damages for consumers. Finnegan said the suit did not make claims of health problems related to AgriGeneral's eggs.
